The absence of metabolic, infectious, toxic, or genetic red flags — combined with the subacute or insidious onset (implied by “recurrent episodes” and functional impairment) — further elevates autoimmune epilepsy on the differential over idiopathic or genetic generalized epilepsies. While video-EEG monitoring remains gold standard for definitive classification, the convergence of semiology, EEG localization, and negative alternative workup makes *autoimmune-associated focal epilepsy* the most biologically plausible and clinically urgent diagnosis — not merely “cryptogenic,” but *cryptogenic *because* of an undetected immune trigger*. Pending CSF and autoantibody results, this is best conceptualized as *probable autoimmune-mediated right temporal lobe epilepsy*.
